name: describe_patch
title: Describe patch
description: Describe the current patch in the ModularSynth rack: modules (id, type, settings, "bypass": true when bypassed), cables ("moduleId:port" → "moduleId:port"), polyphony and whether the clock is running. Call it first.

name: list_module_types
title: List module types
description: List the module types you can add, with their inputs, outputs and settings (name, min, max, default, unit). Pass a type to get just that one. Audio and control signals are voltages: pitch is 1 V per octave (0 V = C4), gates are 0/10 V. Drums can be synthesized with modules, the modular way (kick: a sine VCO whose pitch drops fast, through a VCA with a short envelope; snare: noise through a band-pass VCF with a brief envelope; hi-hat: noise high-passed, very short — see the "Noise percussion" preset), or played by samplers from the built-in kit (list_sounds, set_sample) for a quick result; both are triggered by a Trigger Seq. Choose from what the user asks for. Real instruments and voices (saxophone, vocals…) can’t be synthesized convincingly: use a sampler with a recording the user drops on it (or one of their saved sounds), or audioin (the user’s microphone or line input).

name: list_presets
title: List presets
description: List the ready-made presets (name and what they do). Load one with load_preset to start from a working sound.

name: load_preset
title: Load preset
description: Replace the rack with a ready-made preset, by name (see list_presets). The user can undo it.

name: new_patch
title: New patch
description: Replace the rack with the default starter patch (keyboard → oscillator → filter → amplifier → output). The user can undo it.

name: add_module
title: Add module
description: Add a module to the rack. Optional row and x (in HP) place it; otherwise it goes to the first free spot. Optional params set its knobs. Returns its id. Drums: synthesize them with modules (VCO, Noise, VCF, ADSR, VCA) or load the built-in kit into samplers with set_sample. For a real instrument or a voice, a sampler with the user’s recording, or audioin for a microphone.

name: remove_module
title: Remove module
description: Remove a module and its cables from the rack.

name: connect
title: Connect
description: Patch a cable from an output to an input, both written "moduleId:port". An input takes one cable: plugging into a busy input replaces its cable.

name: disconnect
title: Disconnect
description: Unplug the cable going into an input ("moduleId:port").

name: set_param
title: Set param
description: Turn a knob or flip a switch on a module. The value is clamped to the setting range; the value actually set is returned.

name: set_bypass
title: Set bypass
description: Bypass a module (on: true) or turn it back on (on: false), without unplugging anything: effects and processors (filters, VCA, mixers, delay, reverb…) pass their input straight through; sources and modulators (oscillators, LFO, envelopes, sequencers, clock…) go silent. Output, Scope and Memo can’t be bypassed. Useful to hear a part of a rich patch more clearly; the user can undo it.

name: set_notes
title: Set notes
description: Write the notes of one page (A–D, default A) of a Note Grid sequencer; the other pages are kept. Each note: start step (0–63: sixteenth notes when clocked by Clock ×4, thirty-second notes when the Note Grid "resolution" setting is 1), length in steps, MIDI pitch (60 = C4), optional velocity. Replaces the notes of that page. Only the page selected by the "page" setting plays: put a verse on A and a chorus on B, then save scenes with different "page" values.

name: play_notes
title: Play notes
description: Play notes live, as if on the keyboard (the patch must have a MIDI→CV module wired to sound, its KEYBOARD screen set to All or Computer). Each note: MIDI pitch (60 = C4), start and duration in seconds from now, optional velocity. Up to 64 notes within 30 seconds.

name: save_scene
title: Save scene
description: Save the current settings and sequences of every module as a scene (like a snapshot: intro, verse, chorus, break…), or overwrite an existing scene. Up to 16 scenes. Tempo and the clock's run state are not part of scenes. Returns the scene id.

name: recall_scene
title: Recall scene
description: Switch to a saved scene, like pressing its button: on the next bar while the sound plays, right away otherwise. Stops the song if it was playing.

name: set_song
title: Set song
description: Write the song: scenes played one after another, each for a number of bars (e.g. intro 4, verse 8, chorus 8, break 4, chorus 8). Up to 64 lines; an empty list removes the song. "loop": start again at the end (default true; otherwise the clocks stop). Needs a Clock in the patch to count bars.

name: play_song
title: Play song
description: Play the song from its first line (or from line "from", counted from 0): the scene of each line plays for its bars, clocks restart on the first beat. Stop it with set_transport running: false.

name: highlight
title: Highlight
description: Show the user a module, a knob or a jack by making it glow in the rack for a few seconds (the rack scrolls to it). target: "moduleId", "moduleId:setting" or "moduleId:port". With "to" (an input "moduleId:port") and an output as target, it draws the cable to plug as a dotted line. Use it when you explain or ask the user to turn or patch something.

name: list_sounds
title: List sounds
description: List the sounds a sampler can play: the built-in starter kit (kick, snare, hi-hat, a chord, a pad — always available, made by the synth itself) and the user’s own sounds saved in this browser. Load one with set_sample.

name: set_sample
title: Set sample
description: Load a sound (an id from list_sounds) into a sampler module. Then trigger it with its gate input (from a Trigger Seq, a Note Grid or MIDI→CV) and choose how it plays with set_param "mode": 0 one-shot (drums), 1 hold (plays while the gate is high), 2 loop (synced to the clock).

name: set_transport
title: Set transport
description: Start or stop every Clock in the patch (the ▶/■ button): sequencers play while it runs. Stopping also stops a playing song.

name: undo
title: Undo
description: Undo the last change (yours or the user’s), like Ctrl+Z: first cancels a scene waiting for the next bar, stops a playing song.
